newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian Ramadan - union boss and at least 175 dead.
newsitem.headline: Algerian Ramadan - union boss and at least 175 dead.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas on Tuesday shot dead Algeria's top union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda outside the union headquarters in central Algier, the interior ministry said.

His death followed a rash of bombings and massacres of civilians in Algiers and surrounding towns and hamlets in a relentless guerrilla "Ramadan" violence campaign in which at least 175 other people were killed.
Algerian newspapers have put the death toll at up to 250 in this period, including a 12-year-old boy and five girls who were abducted and had their throats cut near Algiers.
The Moslem fundamentalist Armed Islamic Group had promised to step up attacks during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan which began on January 10.
Following is a list of the main violence in that period:
Jan 12
- Moslem guerrillas kill 14 villagers in Tabainat hamlet, in Blida province, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
-The same day they kidnap five girls and cut their throats in the neighbouring village of Haouch Englise.
Jan 14
- Nine bodies are found in Djebel Koukou in Algiers and Bab Ali village, near Algiers, according to Algerian newspapers.
Jan 16
- At least four guerrillas killed in a seven-hour gunbattle with security forces on the heights of Algiers's ancient Casbah. Residents say more than 10 guerrillas died. Authorities say nothing.
- Bomb explodes in a car market in Boufarik, 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers killing 12 people and wounding scores, according to the authorities. Newspapers put the dead at 14.
Jan 19
- Car bomb explodes on Algiers' Belouizdad Street, Belcourt, killing 21 people and wounding 60, according to the authorities. Newspapers say 42 people were killed.

- Moslem guerrillas kill 36 people in Sidi Abdelaziz village, in Medea province, 70 km (40 miles) south of Algiers, according to the authorities. Newspapers put the toll at 48, with one paper, El Watan, saying 49 died as they were kneeling at prayer in a mosque.
Jan 20
- Bomb explodes by school for girls in an Algiers suburb. No casualties.
Jan 21
- Car bomb explodes in Boulevard des Martyrs, killing six people and wounding 44. Five hours later another blast kills one person near a children's merry-go-round at Boulevard Khelifa Oulmane.
Jan 22
- Bomb explodes in a market in central Blida killing eight and wounding 10, government-controlled El Moudajhid newspaper said.
- Car bomb kills seven and wounds scores in Quatre Chemins hamlet, near Boufarik, according to Liberte newspaper.
Jan 26
- Gunmen kill Said Rabhi, a grassroots activist from hawkish anti-Islamist Rally for Democracy and Culture (RCD) outside his home in Kouba, Algiers.
Jan 28
- Moslem guerrillas shoot dead top union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda by his Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA) headquarters in central Algiers, interior ministry says.
Eyewitnesses said Benhamouda's bodyguard and a union parking area warden were also gunned down.
